subject: Delivery lag: long-running job finalization window & safe-retry proposal
messages:
From: Sarah Kim <sarah@clearmind.ai>
To: Jordan Blake <jordan_blake@redwood.ai>
Cc: Clearmind.ai Contracts <contracts@clearmind.ai>
Date: Tue, 12 Oct 2027 09:14:00 -0700
Subject: Delivery lag observed on nightly inference runs

Hi Jordan,

We saw a spike in 'finalization' latency for our nightly async inference jobs on 2027-10-11 around 02:00 UTC. Roughly 7% of the submitted runs did not report a terminal status within our expected 3-hour window; they eventually completed between 6-12 hours later. This is causing downstream dedup and billing confusion on our side.

Can you confirm whether this is expected behavior under the current contract? If not, we need a remediation plan and a formal exception to the job completion window that we can share internally while we await a permanent fix.

Attached are a sample run log exports and a short list of affected job IDs.

Thanks,
Sarah Kim
Head of ML Ops
Clearmind.ai

Attachments: run-log-sample-20271011.csv
From: Jordan Blake <jordan_blake@redwood.ai>
To: Sarah Kim <sarah@clearmind.ai>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.ai>, Dev Patel <dev_patel@redwood.ai>, Clearmind.ai Contracts <contracts@clearmind.ai>
Date: Tue, 12 Oct 2027 10:02:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Delivery lag observed on nightly inference runs

Hi Sarah — thank you for the logs, and sorry for the disruption. I pulled the trace and flagged this to infra. Quick summary of what we're proposing so you have something to show leadership and procurement while we remediate: 

- Root cause (short): an out-of-bin scheduling regression combined with a KV-cache eviction cascade for a subset of long-sequence jobs. This triggered a small percentage of runs to be retried by the runtime later in the window rather than completing synchronously.

- Immediate customer-facing proposal: we can provide a temporary 12-hour finalization window for the affected job classes (long-seq async runs) as an SLA exception while we deploy a fix. During the exception period we will:
  * Mark jobs submitted in the affected window with a special header so your dedupe can key off it.
  * Emit an explicit final-status webhook at completion (even for delayed completions).
  * Provide a one-off credit backstop if observed late completions cause double-billing within your stack.

- Safe-retry and idempotency guidance (what we'll enable):
  * We will add an idempotency token requirement for multi-chunk async jobs and document the recommended retry-backoff.
  * Server-side dedupe metadata (run-origin-id) will be set in the job status payloads for the exception window.

I'm looping in Marissa (sales) for contractual language and Dev (infra) for the remediation ETA. We attached a draft SLA exception form for review. Please confirm if a 12-hour window is acceptable for your internal stakeholders; if so we'll route the exception form + DocuSign link to Contracts.

—Jordan
Director, Partnerships & GTM
Redwood Inference

Attachments: 20271012-sla-exception-form.pdf
From: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.ai>
To: Jordan Blake <jordan_blake@redwood.ai>, Dev Patel <dev_patel@redwood.ai>
Cc: Sarah Kim <sarah@clearmind.ai>, Clearmind.ai Contracts <contracts@clearmind.ai>
Date: Tue, 12 Oct 2027 13:28:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Delivery lag observed on nightly inference runs

Jordan / Dev — I reviewed this with the CS and finance leads. We can approve a temporary 12-hour finalization-window exemption tied to these conditions:

1) Exception window limited to 30 days from the signed date.
2) Redwood provides a per-run audit CSV within 48 hours for any late-complete jobs (format: run_id, submit_ts, final_ts, status, run-origin-id).
3) If late completions result in duplicate billed units, Redwood issues a credit back to Clearmind within the following billing cycle (documented credit policy to be included in the exception).
4) Engineering to notify Clearmind via webhook + email when the deployment that fixes the eviction cascade is live; auto-retry behavior must be documented.

Dev — can you confirm estimated ETA for the fix and whether the idempotency token change is a minor client-side header or requires SDK patching? If SDK changes are needed, include the version and migration notes in your reply.

Marissa Cole
Sr. Account Lead, Redwood Inference

From: Dev Patel <dev_patel@redwood.ai>
To: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.ai>, Jordan Blake <jordan_blake@redwood.ai>, Sarah Kim <sarah@clearmind.ai>, Clearmind.ai Contracts <contracts@clearmind.ai>
Date: Wed, 13 Oct 2027 11:02:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Delivery lag observed on nightly inference runs

Thanks — quick technical update and action items: 

- ETA: we have a rolling patch scheduled for 2027-10-15 02:00 UTC. That patch prevents the KV eviction cascade and improves scheduling for the long-sequence bin; we expect >99.8% of previously-affected runs to complete within the 3-hour window after deployment.

- Idempotency: we'll accept an idempotency-token header immediately (no SDK change required for customers that set their own headers). For customers using Redwood SDKs, we'll ship a minor patch (v1.14.2) with an opt-in header param. Migration notes: header name X-Redwood-Idempotency, recommended token = client-run-uuid.

- Telemetry & artifacts: we'll generate the per-run audit CSV for any late completions during the exception window and deliver it to your secure S3 bucket.

Next steps:
1) Jordan/Marissa: if Clearmind signs the attached exception form, we'll issue the DocuSign link and schedule the patch as above.
2) Once patch is live, we will monitor three consecutive nightly runs and share the telemetry. If behavior is back to normal, the exception is cancelled early.

—Dev
Principal SRE, Redwood Inference
